payload.description: Use when a question asks how a person was introduced to, started, or first began an activity, interest, hobby, or role. Trigger especially when initial search returns only current or recent activity memories.
content: Expand with origin and temporal phrases: 'since childhood', 'started playing', 'began', 'first started', 'starting with', 'grew up', 'early years', 'first experience with'.
Search for memories describing subject's history over long period: preference, enrichment, state memories.
If first retrieval returns only current events, run follow-up search targeting entry point with life-stage terms.
Check evidence actually explains how introduction happened; if not, continue searching or report absence.
Look for family or mentor references in life-history memories for causal origin.

payload.name: Per-Person Method Coverage
payload.description: Use when a question asks about the ways, methods, tools, or techniques that two or more named people use for a shared activity or routine. Also triggered when expected answer is a union of per-person attributes.
content: Identify every named person and shared activity; run standalone search per person with paraphrase variants.
Method descriptions often use sensory/environmental vocabulary; if initial results lack method-like terms, run additional query with those terms.
If structured filters available, run targeted search for preference-kind memories about each person and activity.
Before answering, verify every named person has at least one retrieved method; if not, run more targeted searches.

payload.name: Per-Subject Coverage for Multi-Person Questions
payload.description: Use when a question asks about experiences, events, or attributes of multiple named individuals, especially when the question implies multiple instances. Also use if initial search returns results for only some of the named people.
content: Identify every named individual in the question. If more than one person is named, treat each as a separate retrieval target.

Run a dedicated search for each named individual separately (e.g., '[Person name] [topic keyword]'), even if a combined search already returned results. Do not rely only on a combined query or on a per-person search for just one of the people.

When the question uses a plural (e.g., 'health scares', 'incidents', 'issues'), check whether there may be multiple relevant memories per person. If the per-person search returns only one memory and the question implies multiple, issue additional query variants (synonyms, related events, time-windowed searches) to surface other memories.
If a per-person search returns a list at the top_k limit, increase depth or top_k, or refine with additional keywords, to avoid missing lower-ranked but relevant memories for that person.

Before answering, explicitly verify that every named individual has at least one supporting memory. If any person is missing evidence, continue searching for that person rather than finalizing the answer with incomplete coverage.

payload.name: Recurring Pattern Concrete Search
payload.description: Use when a question asks about a person's recurring frustration, problem, complaint, or ongoing difficulty, and initial searches with abstract emotion word return weak results.
content: Do not search only with abstract noun plus person's name; target memory may state pattern concretely.
Generate concrete candidate objects/actions and run searches with frequency indicators: 'weekly', 'every week', 'constantly', 'repeatedly', 'ritual', 'keeps'.
After retrieving one supporting memory, check for more recent or explicit version via structured search.

payload.name: Related-Activity Expansion for Practice-Bound Questions
payload.description: Use when a question asks about music, tracks, albums, or similar items a person uses during a practice/activity, or when initial search returns a partial set of such items.
content: Identify activity and list closely related activities or contexts.
Run additional searches pairing person's name with each related activity plus item terms and verbs like 'recommended', 'prefers', 'listens to'.
Treat recommendation/preference memories as evidence for queried activity even if activity name absent.
Before finalizing, verify searches across related activities and review relevant recommendation memories.

payload.name: Related-Context Music Recall
payload.description: Use when a question asks for music pieces, songs, albums, or artists associated with a person and an activity (yoga, meditation, workout), especially if multiple items are implied or first search returns only one explicit item.
content: Expand activity with semantically adjacent terms: for yoga use meditation, relaxation, calming, mindfulness; for workout use exercise, training, focus.
Run complementary searches using each expanded activity term joined with person's name and music-related verb/noun.
Check if any recalled memory mentions recommendation for closely related activity; treat as candidate evidence.
If relevant recommendation found but original query terms did not match, perform verification search using item's entity type and related activity term.

payload.name: Concrete Search for Shared Experiences
payload.description: Use when a question asks about a shared feeling, frustration, problem, or experience between two named people. Also use when initial search for abstract relational phrase returns no direct evidence.
content: Decompose abstract relational questions into concrete per-person searches. For 'What is a shared frustration regarding X for A and B?', search separately for events about A and about B that relate to X, such as 'A searching for X', 'B unable to find X', 'A has not found X'.

Include the concrete domain/object from the question in the query and keywords (e.g., 'pet-friendly spot', 'dog ownership', 'housing', 'shipping problem'), not just the abstract words like 'frustration' or 'shared'.

If the initial hybrid search does not return memories that explicitly describe the emotion or outcome (e.g., 'not found', 'cannot find', 'frustrated'), run at least one follow-up search combining one person's name with the concrete object/action (e.g., 'Andrew pet-friendly spot') with a higher top_k, and inspect event memories that only describe the situation without labeling it as a frustration.

For sufficiency: if one person's event describes a blocked goal (e.g., searching and failing to find) and the other person is involved or concerned with the same topic, treat that as evidence of a shared experience even if the word 'frustration' never appears.

payload.name: Shared with + Month Window Search
payload.description: When a question uses a sharing verb between two people (share/shared with/tell/told/mention) together with a month or year phrase like 'in January 2024', the expected answer often lives in an event memory about only the sharer, and the time should be treated as a range, not a point. Use this Skill to avoid over-restricting queries to memories containing both people or to a single date.
content: Identify the sharer X and recipient Y in the question; for example, 'John' (sharer) and 'Tim' (recipient) in 'What achievement did John share with Tim in January 2024?'

Do not require Y or both names in the retrieved memory — 'shared with' may mean X disclosed or told about an event, so the memory can describe an event about X alone. Formulate at least one query without Y, e.g., 'achievement of X' plus the topic/object hint, keeping the sharer X as the subject.

Parse month/year mentions like 'in January 2024' as a date range (start = first day, end = last day) and use time_mode 'range', not a point at the 1st of the month, because events later in the month would otherwise be filtered out.

If semantic/BM25/keyword results lack a suitable X-only event, run a structured search over memory fields with subject = X, appropriate memory_kinds (e.g., 'event'), and the month range; do not declare 'No information available' until this strategy has been attempted.

payload.name: Skill-Sharing Query Expansion
payload.description: Use when a question asks what skills, recipes, techniques, or knowledge a person taught, shared, or helped others learn. Trigger when initial search returns only the person's own activities.
content: Reformulate query with parallel phrasings not using 'skills': 'shared tips on', 'taught others to', 'showed others how to', 'helped others improve at', 'gave advice on', 'passed on knowledge of', 'mentored'.
Use structured or semantic search targeting 'helped', 'shared', 'taught', 'advised', and social-interaction events.
If top results lack explicit sharing/teaching, perform additional search with tip/teaching synonyms.
Verify each claimed skill has supporting memory clause showing sharing, teaching, or helping.

payload.name: Supplementary Activity Enumeration
payload.description: Use when a question asks what a person does to supplement, enhance, support, or add to their main activity or training routine, or when question requests a list of activities/practices around a recurring topic.
content: Treat 'what does [person] do to supplement/enhance/support [primary activity]' as a list question.
After initial hybrid search, run additional structured or keyword search using person's name combined with general activity-type terms.
Only finalize after examining all retrieved activity-type memories; if only one distinct activity found, explicitly search for parallel or synonymous activities.
Every distinct activity in final answer must be supported by at least one retrieved memory version.

payload.name: Temporal-Neighbor Activity Retrieval
payload.description: Use when a question asks what someone did after or in response to a specific event, and the initial memory search returns an event memory but no direct activity memory. The desired activity often resides in a memory with the same or adjacent world_start date as the event, without sharing the event's keywords.
content: 1. Identify the anchor memory that matches the event named in the question (e.g., the memory describing the person reading the story). Record its world_start timestamp and subject.

2. If the initial results contain no memory stating the post-event action, run a supplementary structured/time-filtered search for the same subject with world_start equal to the anchor's date (or within ±1 day if time of day unknown). Use a query that names the expected activity type (e.g., 'activity', 'visited', 'plan', 'next') rather than reusing the full natural-language question.

3. If no direct hit, inspect the anchor memory's version with include_sources=true and examine other memories originating from the same source/turn, as they may describe the immediately following action.

4. Treat a same-timestamp memory from the same subject as strong candidate evidence for 'after the event'; include it in the answer only if its content describes an action attributable to the person and plausibly follows the event.

payload.name: Time_And_Purpose_Constrained_Retrieval
payload.description: Use when a question asks what a specific person shared, posted, photographed, made, or created during an explicit month or period (e.g., 'in November 2022'), especially when the activity is described with a purpose like 'experimentation' or 'trying something new'. Trigger when initial search results are dominated by memories of other times or semantically similar but unrelated topics.
content: If the question specifies a month or year, apply a structured time filter on world_start (treating world_end as unbounded) in the search request; do not rely solely on the date appearing as free-text keywords in the query.

When the question involves an action like 'shared a photo of', 'posted about', or 'made', and the stated purpose is vague (e.g., 'experimentation'), expand with purpose synonyms and rerun the search using the person's name plus terms such as 'shared', 'photo', 'made', 'cooked', 'created', 'experimented with', 'new recipe', or 'tried'.

Before answering, verify that the candidate memory explicitly satisfies the full constraint set: subject (the asked-about person), action (shared/posted/photographed/created), time period (world_start falls within the asked window), and purpose/activity (e.g., an experiment or new attempt). A memory that matches only a semantic topic or only a partial timeframe is not sufficient evidence.

If a particular topic (e.g., the person's pets) keeps dominating results but fails the time or purpose check, suppress that topic in subsequent searches (e.g., exclude its keywords) and deliberately search for other recent activities of the person within the requested time window.
